section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the connection between the two interpretations of "Atah Hareisa Lada'as," where knowledge of the immanent light leads to knowledge of the Awtsmoos through the revelation of His capacity.
section.t: Based on this, we can also explain the connection between the two interpretations
(above, section 4)
of "Atah Hareisa Lada'as,"
that "Atah Hareisa Lada'as" is the knowledge of the One Who fills all worlds, and that "Atah Hareisa Lada'as" is the knowledge of the Awtsmoos
(to know You),
for the knowledge and contemplation of the light that is invested in the worlds
(the light that fills)
is primarily so that even the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis will know G-dliness,
and this—that even the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis can comprehend G-dliness
(and in a manner that through this it will come to self-nullification,
contrary to its nature)—
is through the revelation of the capacity of the Awtsmoos,
through which even darkness is transformed into light.
For this knowledge is in the power of the Awtsmoos,
but the knowledge itself is only in the light that fills.
And after this knowledge,
there must be the knowledge and contemplation of the surrounding light
[for this is the commandment "and you shall know," etc.,
as above in section 4],
and that the light that fills, which is invested in the worlds, is merely an illumination that is incomparable relative to the Ein Sof that is above the worlds
(the surrounding light),
and then specifically it is appropriate to contemplate and know the advantage in the knowledge of the light that fills, which is understood even in the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
that this knowledge is from the aspect of the capacity of the Awtsmoos,
as above.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the purpose of the emanation of knowledge in the Awtsmoos itself is for the sake of the knowledge of G-dliness in created beings, which elevates that knowledge.
section.t: Based on this, we can also explain what was brought above
(section 5)
from the discourses,
that He, blessed be He, emanated the matter of knowledge in His Awtsmoos so that through this there could be knowledge of G-dliness in creations,
for from this—that the intention in the emanation of knowledge in His Awtsmoos is so that creations will know G-dliness—
it is understood
that there is an advantage in this knowledge
(that creations know G-dliness)
over the knowledge in His Awtsmoos.
And it is like the explanation in Tanya
that the purpose of the chain of descent of the worlds is not for the sake of the higher worlds,
since for them it is a descent from the light of His countenance,
and the purpose of the higher worlds is that through them this lower world is brought into being,
through which the intention of a dwelling place in the lower realms is fulfilled,
a dwelling place for the Awtsmoos.
And thus,
this matter in the higher worlds—
that through them this lower world is brought into being—
is more elevated than the higher worlds themselves.
For the higher worlds themselves are in the category of descent,
and that through them this lower world is brought into being
is their elevation.
And similarly, regarding the emanation of knowledge in His Awtsmoos,
the knowledge is like a descent from the light of His countenance
[for even though this emanation of knowledge is in His Awtsmoos,
nevertheless,
relative to the Awtsmoos as it is in itself
(before He emanated the knowledge),
the knowledge is a descent],
and the purpose of the emanation of knowledge is that through it there will be knowledge of G-dliness in the creations,
even in the intellect of the Nefesh HaBahamis,
through which the capacity of the Awtsmoos is revealed,
and through the drawing down from His own knowledge to the knowledge of G-dliness in the creations,
an elevation is made, so to speak, in His own knowledge.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section describes the elevation in the knowledge of the Awtsmoos through the knowledge of G-dliness in creations, analogous to the foot elevating the head, and the revelation of "Ein Od Milvado" through the joy of the hakafos.
section.t: And it can be said
that the elevation that is made in His own knowledge through the knowledge of G-dliness in the creations is analogous to the influence from the foot to the head,
from the aspect that the root of the foot is above the head,
"their end is interwoven in their beginning."
For this matter still pertains to the order of the chain of descent.
And there is another matter in "Atah Hareisa Lada'as,"
that through the knowledge of G-dliness of the creations, there is drawn
(afterwards)
the revelation of "Ein Od Milvado,"
the capacity of the Awtsmoos.
And this is that before the hakafos we say "Atah Hareisa Lada'as... Ein Od Milvado,"
which is an explanation of the great elevation of the joy of the hakafos.
For this—that the joy is in a manner that the feet lift and elevate the head—
its intention is regarding the head of man and the head in every level and level,
up to the level of His own knowledge.
And furthermore,
that through the dancing of Simchas Torah, there is drawn the aspect of the makif that is above the boundaries of head and foot,
up to the revelation of "Ein Od Milvado,"
the capacity of the Awtsmoos.
